When should I use BBDBuy purchasing instead of parcel forwarding?

Use purchasing when you still need someone to buy an item from the seller. Forwarding starts with an item you have already acquired. Submitting both for one purchase can create a second order that you never intended.
Which address should I give a seller when forwarding an item?

Copy the current receiving address and identifying information from your own BBDBuy account. Preserve the required recipient details. Someone else's warehouse screenshot can point to the wrong account even when the street address looks familiar.
What belongs in a forwarding notice for a carton containing several items?

List each item, its quantity and identifying details. Retain the domestic courier name and tracking number for the outer carton. A list of contents makes a mismatch easier to investigate when several small pieces share one label.
What if the merchant sends two boxes under separate tracking numbers?
Keep a separate domestic tracking record for each box and ask how to register both against your account. Match each arrival to the expected contents before assuming the second box is missing.
Which number should I use when asking about an outbound parcel?
Quote the outbound parcel reference and, if available, its international tracking number. Include the purchase or forwarding reference for a particular item only when the question concerns that item.
How do I check the quantity on a multipack listing?

Read the selected option for the unit of sale. If the option contains three pairs and the order quantity is two, you expect six pairs. Check whether the unit price covers the pack before multiplying a second time.
What if the colour I need is sold only as part of a set?
Open the exact seller option and record how many pieces of each colour it contains. Ask whether substitutions are acceptable before payment when the option description and photograph disagree.
Why does the product total change when I select another option?
Some listings group an accessory, a single piece and a complete set together. Read the price after selecting the intended option. Keep its text, quantity and subtotal with your payment record.
What should I save before accepting a price adjustment?
Keep the original selection and amount, the revised seller amount, the currency and the explanation for the change. If postage or another service was added, record it separately from the unit price.
Does a warehouse arrival notice prove the contents are complete?

An intake event concerns the package or entry displayed. Compare the expected option and quantity with its recorded contents or inspection pictures. Name any missing component when asking for a warehouse check.
How can I match a QC picture to one of two similar purchases?

Use the order reference, colour name and size label together. Distinctive hardware or trim can help identify a version. The same promotional shot on two seller pages gives you no way to tell which unit arrived.
Should I keep a shoebox for an intended gift?

Decide whether the box itself is part of what the recipient needs. Ask how it will be protected and whether it affects return conditions. Compare the packed dimensions of the available alternatives before choosing.
Which dimensions go into a shipping comparison?
Use the outside length, width and height of the packed parcel, with a consistent unit. A manufacturer's product dimensions omit the carton and protection, so they describe a different object.
Why do two available lines give different totals for the same box?
Check their weight rules, increments, destination coverage and optional services. Compare the all-in figures displayed for the same parcel and distinguish a route restriction from a change in price.
How should I record a charge covering more than one order?
Keep a single parcel-level entry for a shared freight or packing charge. If you divide it between items for budgeting, label that division as your allocation so it does not appear twice in the total.
What evidence helps with a refund enquiry?

Group the order reference, paid amount, selected option, evidence of the issue and seller response. Identify whether you are asking about approval, the refund amount or receipt of funds; each is a different question.
How to read a BBDBuy payment record when an order has several charges

One payment can cover two products, while a later payment can cover freight for products bought on different days. A running total in your bank app does not tell you the cost of an individual purchase. Start with the event each payment paid for.
Start with the unit you actually bought

Suppose you choose two identical packs of socks. The seller's option says three pairs per pack. In your notebook, record two packs, six pairs expected and the price per pack. The distinction matters twice. It gives you the quantity to expect at intake and it keeps you from multiplying the pack price by six. If the seller also offers a single pair, save the text beside the price after you choose the pack.

Open the confirmation and copy its reference. Put the seller link on the same line. If a single payment covers several order lines, keep one payment reference and list its component orders beneath it. A photo of a bank charge can help later, but the descriptive details on the order are what connect money to a particular item.
Separate payment stages before assigning costs

A purchasing request and a parcel submission pay for different work. The BBDBuy ordering and forwarding guide distinguishes the cost of acquiring the product from forwarding a parcel. In practice, build one group of lines for the seller purchase and domestic delivery and a second for the outbound parcel. Add packing or optional services only where the confirmation actually lists them. Leave an unknown charge blank until you have the record.

Imagine two seller charges of 80 and 120 in the same currency with one shared domestic charge of 10. Their purchase subtotal is 210. Counting 10 on each item produces 220 and makes the later parcel look more expensive than it was. If you want a per-item estimate for your own budget, split the 10 equally or proportionally and note the method. The seller still charged one amount.
Record a price change without rewriting history

Suppose the first order showed 80 and a later request shows 86. Save the old and new figures, selected option and reason given. Six more for the same product is a different issue from a six-unit delivery adjustment. Ask which changed if the message is unclear. Preserve your original note until the agent confirms the final purchase or cancellation.

A pending card authorization and a completed payment can appear together temporarily. Compare transaction status, amounts and merchant reference before adding them as separate purchases. If the order page still shows unpaid, check the payment history and ask about the specific reference before submitting a second payment. A screenshot showing both entries is more useful with their status and dates visible.
Reconcile the final parcel and any credit

When you submit several items together, enter the outbound freight once against the parcel number. Keep the item-to-parcel mapping alongside it. If you compare an estimate and final charge, use the chosen route, destination and actual packed measurements. The price recorded on a spreadsheet card is not a useful comparison for that second payment.

For a returned item, add a credit as its own event with date, currency and destination. A credit shown in an agent balance and a refund to your payment instrument have different destinations. Leave the expected refund open until you can identify the actual entry. The complete trail should explain what you paid, what you received and the net amount still attributed to the order.
A worked purchase with a later refund and one shared parcel

Take an illustrative order for two medium work shirts and a separate order for a cap. Assume the confirmation lists the shirts at 75 each and a single domestic delivery charge of 12. The purchase subtotal is 162. The cap costs 38 with domestic delivery included, bringing the amount paid for the two purchases to 200 in the same currency. At this point both purchase records can be closed as paid even though there is no figure yet for the journey from the warehouse to your home.

Now imagine the seller can supply only one shirt. You might expect a credit of 75, the unused unit price. Whether some domestic delivery is credited must be checked against the actual agreement. If the seller delivers one shirt for the originally quoted domestic fee and a credit of 75 really is recorded, the net cost of the goods and domestic delivery becomes 125. Keep the original 162 payment intact in the record. Replacing it with 87 conceals the transaction you will need if the credit is delayed.

Suppose the single shirt and cap are later packed into one outbound parcel. Freight is 46 and a separately itemized packing choice is 4. Add a parcel payment of 50. The total cash out across the original payments is 250, with 75 credited, yielding a net of 175. The items have purchase records of 162 and 38, the parcel has a payment of 50, and the credit has a reference of its own. Those four numbers give you a way to reproduce the result without guessing what any bank entry meant.

If you want to compare the cost of the cap with a local alternative, you still need to decide how to allocate the shared parcel cost. An equal split attributes 25 to the cap. A split by measured weight might attribute much less. Neither division appears on the carrier invoice unless the invoice actually itemizes freight per piece. Keep a column labelled personal allocation. It allows another person to understand how you reached the comparison without mistaking your method for a charge imposed by BBDBuy.
Trace discrepancies from the record outward

First check for a missing stage. If your budget shows 125 and the parcel payment has not yet been collected, the budget may correctly reflect goods in the warehouse but cannot describe the final delivered cost. If it shows 250 after a confirmed credit, inspect where the 75 was credited. It might still be available in an account balance rather than represented by a bank entry. Record how that balance can be used and do not count it again when reviewing a later purchase paid from it.

Next distinguish balance funding from spending an existing balance. Moving 100 onto an account and then using 80 of it toward a purchase moves money into the account once. Adding both as if they were separate product costs gives a misleading 180. Record the funding event as a transfer between places where you track money. Record the order as spending from that balance. Check any conversion or payment charges separately against their displayed currency and reference.

Finally examine cancelled attempts and split payments. A buyer may cover part of an order with an existing balance and the rest by a payment method. In that case the single order subtotal can correspond to two funding entries. Compare the sum of the confirmed entries with the amount due. Keep a failed or reversed attempt visible as an exception until its final status is known, but do not silently add it to merchandise cost.
Send an enquiry another person can answer

A useful payment message identifies one unresolved difference. For the example above it might ask where the 75 credit from the unavailable shirt was posted, quoting the purchase reference and date of the message approving it. That is easier to investigate than a general claim that the order cost more than expected. Include an image of the relevant confirmation if needed, showing the item, amount and reference while excluding unrelated financial details.

Once the discrepancy is resolved, record the answer beside the original number. Future comparisons should say whether they include the amount spent, the amount refunded or the remaining balance. This matters months later when one shipment contains several purchases and the original seller page no longer displays the same offer.
